Business & Education Partnership Update - (Youth Creativity Fund & Youth Empowerment Day)
notes:
April Albano, Executive Director of the Business & Education Partnership (BEP), provided a presentation on the Youth Creativity Fund & Youth Empowerment Day. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. She introduced the work of BEP which is a non-profit dedicated to helping youth in Waterloo Region build their path to rewarding careers in partnership with caregivers, educators and industry. She also highlighted the positive feedback from the youth participants in the program which included improved self-esteem and confidence and development in areas such as creativity, problem solving, and leadership skills. 

Responding to Council, A. Albano confirmed that BEP is working with both the public and Catholic school boards and are investigating potential avenues for expansion of the program. She further confirmed that typically grants are given in amounts ranging from $500 to $1000 and there have been 158 grants provided to creative youth projects since 2023.

items.title: Catherine Clarridge, Kitchener
notes: C. Clarridge provided a lived experience account of her previous encounters with housing services and waterloo police services in the Region of Waterloo. She expressed concerns related to the treatment of unhoused individuals specifically those that have endured violent acts and those with limited access to supports. She expressed further concerns with the responsiveness and accountability of municipal, housing, and police leaders.

items.title: Benjamin Hesch, CEO, Woolwich Community Health Centre
notes:
B. Hesch, Chief Executive Officer of the Woolwich Community Health Centre (WCHC), requested that the Region of Waterloo provide a grant of $81,681.86, equal to the Regional Development Charge already applied to WCHC’s facility expansion. This represents 50% of the outstanding expansion cost. He highlighted the current services being provided to the rural health units and the necessary expansion to continue to provide needs community supports. 

Responding to Council, B. Hesch confirmed that the timing of the grant funding is critical because the construction project is nearing completion and development charges have been paid.

Council discussed the funding of health units in the Townships and that Council supporting health care has been an historical occurrence. Dr. H. Wang, Commissioner Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, confirmed that there have been several previous funding collaborations with the WCHC and their continued work with the province.

items.title: Eric O’Grady, North Dumfries
notes:
E. O'Grady provided a delegation on the litter caused by open recycling bins being impacted by weather and a potential solution referred to as BinNet. He showed a demonstration video of the product illustrating how residents can use this to limit litter around the community. He highlighted that there the litter from recycling bins has a negative impact to both the environment and the taxpayer as staff have been tasked will community clean-up.

Responding to Council, E. O'Grady confirmed that he has not reached out directly to the province as there have been various barriers when communicating with Circular Materials on the matter.

Darshpreet Bhatti, CAO, confirmed that he will connect Waste Management staff with E. O'Grady to further discussions with Circular Materials.

items.title: A&F Summary - September 8, 2026
notes:
Council considered each motion separately to allow for discussion and debate. Council did not speak to the first motion but did thank staff for the update to the GRAAC terms of reference listed under the second motion.

Responding to questions related to the third motion, K. Tupil confirmed that the tax stabilization reserve is approximately $16 million, however, the recommended reserve amount is a minimum of $20 million. 

Council discussed the association with the requested amount being related to development charges and debated modifying the funding cost to differ it from the mirrored development charges amount. The recommended motion with the deferral language was amended to remove the deferral and the requested funding was approved.

Other Business
notes: Council recognized that 2026 marks a once-in-a-lifetime milestone for the Royal Canadian Legion. Founded in 1925 at the Unity Conference, the Legion began with a clear mission to support Veterans, advocate for their rights, and ensure the act of Remembrance continues. On July 17, 1926, the Legion was officially incorporated by a special Act of Parliament. The Legion has had a century of standing with Veterans, strengthening communities, and honouring the memory of those who served.

motions.text: The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Response Time Performance Plan (RTPP) for 2027, outlined below, in accordance with the Ambulance Act, O. Reg. 257/00, under Part VIII, Response Time Standards, as amended by O. Reg. 251/25, s. 5, as outlined in PHP-PSV-26-005, dated September 8, 2026. Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) – 6 minutes or less 70% of the time. (Note: Ministry of Health target is 50%.) CTAS 1 – 8 minutes or less 70% of the time. CTAS 2 – 10 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 3 – 15 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 4 – 20 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 5 – 25 minutes or less 80% of the time. Whereas the Region of Waterloo is responsible for funding and coordinating homelessness services, including emergency shelters, supportive and transitional housing, and outreach programming; and Whereas Council has a responsibility to ensure that new investments in housing and homelessness services do not unintentionally reinforce geographic inequities but instead contribute to a more balanced and accessible regional system; and Whereas the Region's commitment to addressing homelessness must include, not only increasing overall capacity, but also ensuring equitable access to services across all municipalities, including a more equitable distribution of funding and services dedicated specifically to women; and Whereas there are only 20 emergency homeless shelter beds for women in Cambridge, 42 total throughout the entire Region and only 80 of all shelter beds dedicated to men are in Cambridge while the remaining 130 are in Kitchener-Waterloo; 120 all gender beds in Kitchener-Waterloo and Whereas the single women’s shelter in Cambridge has been forced to deny almost 300 requests for services due to consistently being at capacity since August 2025; and Whereas residents experiencing homelessness in Cambridge are frequently required to travel outside their community to access shelter and other homelessness supports services, creating additional barriers to safety, continuity of care, and connection to local supports; and Whereas Porchlight Counselling and Addiction Services’ winter warming centre for men operated at a minimum of 128% and maximum of 198% throughout its 2025-6 seasonal operations and their request to operate this centre 365 days a year was rejected by the Region, the reason given being a lack of funding; and Whereas Thrive HIV Prevention and Support, which operates the Multi Agency Community Space out of 150 Main in Cambridge - the single drop-in space for individuals experiencing homelessness in Cambridge - is only funded to operate during afternoons, despite an immense need for extended operating hours; and Whereas YWCA Cambridge has requested that the Region fund a 365-day, low-barrier overnight drop-in for women in Cambridge and been repeatedly told there is not adequate funding to do so, despite the lack of any overnight spaces for women in Cambridge existing outside of the 20-bed shelter; and Whereas the Region recently granted Kitchener a 365-day, 22.5-hr-a-day shelter; and Whereas such recent funding decisions only further concentrate services in one city and predominantly on programs dedicated to men or which are co-ed, while neglecting to address the immense lack of services in Cambridge; and Whereas research consistently shows that women avoid co-ed spaces out of fear for their safety, effectively rendering co-ed spaces for men only, further exacerbating the discrepancy in service availability for men versus women; Therefore, Be It Resolved That Regional Council direct staff to bring a report to the November 2026 Community & Health Services Committee with recommendations related to: the principle that major investments in homelessness and infrastructure be accompanied by a strategy to improve service access and capacity in underserved municipalities; and future homelessness-related capital funding allocations exceeding 1 million include an assessment of geographic distribution impacts and a requirement to identify complementary investments in underserved municipalities where gaps exist; and improving homelessness service capacity and access in underserved municipalities, including Cambridge, as part of future homelessness system planning and capital budget deliberations; and the application of Gender-Based Analysis Plus lens to all investments in homelessness and infrastructure to ensure a gender equitable distribution in funding and services across the Region of Waterloo.
motions.text_html:
The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Response Time Performance Plan (RTPP) for 2027, outlined below, in accordance with the Ambulance Act, O. Reg. 257/00, under Part VIII, Response Time Standards, as amended by O. Reg. 251/25, s. 5, as outlined in PHP-PSV-26-005, dated September 8, 2026.
    1. Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) – 6 minutes or less 70% of the time. (Note: Ministry of Health target is 50%.)
    2. CTAS 1 – 8 minutes or less 70% of the time.
    3. CTAS 2 – 10 minutes or less 80% of the time.
    4. CTAS 3 – 15 minutes or less 80% of the time.
    5. CTAS 4 – 20 minutes or less 80% of the time.
    6. CTAS 5 – 25 minutes or less 80% of the time.

  2. Whereas the Region of Waterloo is responsible for funding and coordinating homelessness services, including emergency shelters, supportive and transitional housing, and outreach programming; and

    Whereas Council has a responsibility to ensure that new investments in housing and homelessness services do not unintentionally reinforce geographic inequities but instead contribute to a more balanced and accessible regional system; and

    Whereas the Region's commitment to addressing homelessness must include, not only increasing overall capacity, but also ensuring equitable access to services across all municipalities, including a more equitable distribution of funding and services dedicated specifically to women; and

    Whereas there are only 20 emergency homeless shelter beds for women in Cambridge, 42 total throughout the entire Region and only 80 of all shelter beds dedicated to men are in Cambridge while the remaining 130 are in Kitchener-Waterloo; 120 all gender beds in Kitchener-Waterloo and

    Whereas the single women’s shelter in Cambridge has been forced to deny almost 300 requests for services due to consistently being at capacity since August 2025; and

    Whereas residents experiencing homelessness in Cambridge are frequently required to travel outside their community to access shelter and other homelessness supports services, creating additional barriers to safety, continuity of care, and connection to local supports; and

    Whereas Porchlight Counselling and Addiction Services’ winter warming centre for men operated at a minimum of 128% and maximum of 198% throughout its 2025-6 seasonal operations and their request to operate this centre 365 days a year was rejected by the Region, the reason given being a lack of funding; and

    Whereas Thrive HIV Prevention and Support, which operates the Multi Agency Community Space out of 150 Main in Cambridge - the single drop-in space for individuals experiencing homelessness in Cambridge - is only funded to operate during afternoons, despite an immense need for extended operating hours; and 

    Whereas YWCA Cambridge has requested that the Region fund a 365-day, low-barrier overnight drop-in for women in Cambridge and been repeatedly told there is not adequate funding to do so, despite the lack of any overnight spaces for women in Cambridge existing outside of the 20-bed shelter; and

    Whereas the Region recently granted Kitchener a 365-day, 22.5-hr-a-day shelter; and

    Whereas such recent funding decisions only further concentrate services in one city and predominantly on programs dedicated to men or which are co-ed, while neglecting to address the immense lack of services in Cambridge; and

    Whereas research consistently shows that women avoid co-ed spaces out of fear for their safety, effectively rendering co-ed spaces for men only, further exacerbating the discrepancy in service availability for men versus women;

    Therefore, Be It Resolved That Regional Council direct staff to bring a report to the November 2026 Community & Health Services Committee with recommendations related to:

  • the principle that major investments in homelessness and infrastructure be accompanied by a strategy to improve service access and capacity in underserved municipalities; and
  • future homelessness-related capital funding allocations exceeding 1 million include an assessment of geographic distribution impacts and a requirement to identify complementary investments in underserved municipalities where gaps exist; and
  • improving homelessness service capacity and access in underserved municipalities, including Cambridge, as part of future homelessness system planning and capital budget deliberations; and
  •  the application of Gender-Based Analysis Plus lens to all investments in homelessness and infrastructure to ensure a gender equitable distribution in funding and services across the Region of Waterloo.

WHEREAS the Grand and Speed Rivers create significant natural barriers within Cambridge and concentrate vehicular, pedestrian and cycling movements on a limited number of crossings; AND WHEREAS continued population and employment growth will place additional demands on Cambridge's transportation network and existing river crossings; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT as part of the Region of Waterloo's current review of the Regional road and transportation system, staff be directed to: Assess whether existing Grand and Speed River crossings in Cambridge will provide sufficient capacity and network resiliency to accommodate projected growth to 2051; Assess the need and opportunities for additional vehicular, pedestrian and cycling crossings, including their potential to improve traffic movement, emergency and alternate-route access, active transportation connectivity and overall network resiliency; Review previous studies and assumptions concerning additional river crossings to determine whether they remain appropriate in light of current growth projections, development patterns and transportation demands; Identify any potential future crossing corridors that should be protected through long-term transportation and land-use planning; and Report back to Regional Council with findings and recommendations for consideration in the Region’s long term transportation plans

4. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for improvements to Victoria Street North (Regional Road No. 55) between King Street West and Weber Street West, in the City of Kitchener, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report PDL-LEG-26-040, dated September 8, 2026, described as follows: 
Fee Simple Partial Taking:

i. Part of Lots 63 and 64, Registered Plan 374, being Part 1 on 58R-22506, City of Kitchener, Part of PIN 22317-0012 (LT) (247 Duke Street West, City of Kitchener);

And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the property within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the property, as required by the Expropriations Act;

And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession for the property after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required;

And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001;

And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the property in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act;

And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation;

And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Transportation Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project.

 

5. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the curbside Christmas tree collection program as set out in report EES-WMS-26-003, dated September 8, 2026:

    1. Direct staff to partner with Family and Children’s Services Foundation (FACS Foundation), a local organization, to develop, implement and communicate a curbside Christmas tree fundraiser collection service in Waterloo Region, effective January 2027.
    2. Direct staff to offer a free Christmas tree drop-off service at the Region’s Waste Management sites for two weeks in January each year.
    3. Discontinue the curbside collection of natural Christmas trees provided by the Region’s contractor, Halton Recycling Ltd. dba Emterra Environmental (Emterra), effective January 2027.
    4. Direct staff to amend the waste collection contract (P2023-33 Automated Cart-Based, and Manual Waste Collection, and Supply, Initial Distribution and On-Going Maintenance of Carts) with Emterra to remove the Christmas tree collection service from the contract.

6. WHEREAS the Grand and Speed Rivers create significant natural barriers within Cambridge and concentrate vehicular, pedestrian and cycling movements on a limited number of crossings;

AND WHEREAS continued population and employment growth will place additional demands on Cambridge's transportation network and existing river crossings;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT as part of the Region of Waterloo's current review of the Regional road and transportation system, staff be directed to:

    1. Assess whether existing Grand and Speed River crossings in Cambridge will provide sufficient capacity and network resiliency to accommodate projected growth to 2051;
    2. Assess the need and opportunities for additional vehicular, pedestrian and cycling crossings, including their potential to improve traffic movement, emergency and alternate-route access, active transportation connectivity and overall network resiliency;
    3. Review previous studies and assumptions concerning additional river crossings to determine whether they remain appropriate in light of current growth projections, development patterns and transportation demands;
    4. Identify any potential future crossing corridors that should be protected through long-term transportation and land-use planning; and
    5. Report back to Regional Council with findings and recommendations for consideration in the Region’s long term transportation plans
